skill.name: webask-ab-significance
skill.description: Сравнивает варианты A/B-теста опроса WebAsk и проверяет, реальна ли разница или укладывается в погрешность. Применяется, когда человек спрашивает, какой вариант опроса лучше, или собирается принять решение по итогам теста.
skill.summary: Compare WebAsk survey variants using outcome counts, percentage-point differences, sample-size guidance, and group comparability checks.
skill.author: webaskio

content.value_statement: Small survey samples can make random differences look like meaningful improvements. This skill guides comparisons using outcome counts, percentage-point differences, and checks for comparable groups.
actual_capabilities: Ask which outcome defines success before comparing survey variants.
Request variant-specific survey summaries and reports through get_quiz_summary and get_quiz_report.
Report outcome counts alongside rates and percentage-point differences.
Check whether groups share the same observation period and traffic source.
Apply sample-size guidance and withhold winner recommendations when data is insufficient.
Respond in the user language and report service limits without recommending paid upgrades.
limitations: Requires access to the external WebAsk MCP tools and relevant survey data.
Provides heuristic sample-size guidance, not an implemented statistical test, confidence interval, or power calculation.
Does not define a testing procedure for average ratings or multiple comparisons.
Its no-difference conclusion does not establish statistical equivalence; inconclusive results need careful interpretation.

use_cases.title: Compare survey completion
use_cases.description: Compare completion counts and rates for two survey versions while checking observation periods and traffic sources.

use_cases.title: Review contact collection
use_cases.description: Compare contact submission rates across survey variants without selecting a winner from a small observed difference.

use_cases.title: Assess experiment readiness
use_cases.description: Review whether response counts and group comparability support a decision or require more data.

prompt_templates.title: Compare two variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare variants A and B for WebAsk survey [survey]. Use survey completion as the success metric.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: start a basic survey comparison.

prompt_templates.title: Report conversion differences
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare contact submissions for variants [A] and [B] in survey [survey] during [period]. Show counts, denominators, rates, and percentage-point differences.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: compare a defined outcome over one period.

prompt_templates.title: Check group comparability
prompt_templates.prompt: Review variants [A] and [B] for survey [survey]. Check periods, traffic sources, and sample sizes before interpreting [metric]. Identify missing information.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: evaluate whether the groups support a fair comparison.

prompt_templates.title: Review decision uncertainty
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess whether survey [survey] supports choosing variant [A] or [B] for [metric]. Separate observed differences from statistical evidence. Explain sample-size assumptions and missing inputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a decision summary with explicit uncertainty.

output_examples.input: Compare contact submissions: A has 42 of 180, and B has 34 of 179. Both groups use the same period and source.
output: Variant A: 42 of 180 submitted contact details, or 23.3%.
Variant B: 34 of 179 submitted contact details, or 19.0%.
Observed difference: 4.3 percentage points in favor of A.
These counts alone do not establish a reliable winner. A formal test and sample-size plan are needed before claiming significance.

output_examples.input: A completed 60 of 100 surveys last month from email traffic. B completed 75 of 100 this month from paid traffic.
output: Variant A: 60% completion. Variant B: 75% completion.
Observed difference: 15 percentage points in favor of B.
The periods and traffic sources differ, so the comparison cannot isolate the variant effect.
Compare groups from the same period and traffic source before choosing a winner.

best_practices: Define the success metric and denominator before reviewing variant results.
Compare groups from the same period and traffic source, and retain the underlying counts.
Use a prespecified statistical test and power calculation to validate decisions beyond the skill's sample-size heuristics.
anti_patterns: Declaring a winner from a small percentage difference without considering sample size.
Comparing variants from different periods or traffic sources as if the groups were equivalent.
Repeatedly checking results and stopping as soon as the preferred variant leads.

faq.question: What data does the skill need?
faq.answer: It needs variant exposure counts, completion counts, the chosen success metric, observation periods, and traffic sources.

faq.question: Which tools does it use?
faq.answer: It names get_quiz_summary and get_quiz_report as external WebAsk MCP dependencies for retrieving survey data.

faq.question: Does it calculate formal statistical significance?
faq.answer: The files provide comparison instructions and sample-size heuristics. They do not specify a formal test, significance threshold, or confidence-interval method.

faq.question: Can it determine the exact sample size required?
faq.answer: It asks for a collection estimate but supplies only rough guidance. Exact planning requires assumptions about baseline rate, detectable effect, significance, and power.

faq.question: Can it modify surveys or require an upgrade?
faq.answer: The documented tools read reports and summaries. The instructions prohibit upgrade suggestions and require stopping when service limits prevent progress.

faq.question: Which assistants and languages are supported?
faq.answer: The listing supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. The skill instructs the assistant to respond in the user language.
